verses.t: And it happened, after that Alexander son of Philip, the Macedonian, who came out of the land of Chettum, had smitten Darius king of the Persians and Medes, that he reigned in his stead, the first over Greece,
And made many wars, and wan many strong holds, and slew the kings of the earth,
And went through to the ends of the earth, and tooke spoiles of many nations, insomuch, that the earth was quiet before him, whereupon he was exalted, and his heart was lifted up.
And he gathered a mighty strong hoste, and ruled over countries, and nations and kings, who became tributaries to him.
And after these things he fell sicke, and perceiued that he should die.
Therefore he called his seruants, such as were honourable, and had been brought up with him from his youth, and parted kis kingdom among them, while he was yet aliue:
So Alexander reigned twelue years, and (then) died.
And his seruants bare rule every one in his place.
And after his death they all put crownes so did their sons after them, many years, and euils were multiplied in the earth.

And there came out of them a wicked roote, Antiochus Epiphanes, son of Antiochus the king, who had beene an hostage at Rome, and he reigned in the hundredth and thirty and seuenth year of the kingdom of the Greekes.

In those daies went there out of Israel wicked men, who perswaded many, saying, Let us go, and make a couenant with the heathen, that are round about us: for since we departed from them, we have had much sorrow.
So this deuise pleased them well.
Then certaine of the people were so forward heerein, that they went to the king, who gaue them licence to do after the ordinances of the heathen.
Whereupon they built a place of exercise at Jerusalem, according to the customes of the heathen,
And made themselues, vncircumcised, and forsooke the holy couenant, and ioyned themselues to the heathen, and were sold to do mischiefe.
Now when the kingdom was established, before Antiochus, he thought to reigne over Egypt, that he might have þ dominion of two realms:
Therefore he entred into Egypt with a great multitude, with chariots, and elephants, and horsemen, and a great nauie,
And made warre against Ptolomee king of Egypt, but Ptolomee was afraide of him, and fled: and many were wounded to death.
Thus they got the strong cities in the land of Egypt, and he tooke the spoiles of it.
And after that Antiochus had smitten Egypt, he returned again in the hundredth fortie and third year, and went up against Israel and Jerusalem with a great multitude,
And entred proudly into the sanctuarie, and tooke away the golden altar, and the candlesticke of light, and all the vessels of it,

And the table of the shewbread, and the powring vessels, and the vials, and the censers of gold, & the vaile, and the crownes, & the golden ornaments that were before the temple, all which he pulled off.
He tooke also the siluer and the gold, and the pretious vessels: also he tooke the hidden treasures which he found:
And when he had taken all away, he went into his own land, hauing made a great massacre, and spoken very proudly.
Therfore there was great mourning in Israel, in every place where they were;
So that the Princes and Elders mourned, the virgines and yong men were made feeble, and the beautie of women was changed.
Every bridegrome tooke up lamentation, and she that sate in the marriage chamber, was in heauinesse.
The land also was moued for the inhabitants of it, and all the house of Iacob was couered with confusion.
And after two years fully expired, the king sent his chiefe collectour of tribute to the cities of Iuda, who came to Jerusalem with a great multitude,
And spoke peaceable words to them, but deceit: for when they had given him credence, he fell suddenly upon the city, and smote it very sore, & destroyed much people of Israel.
And when he had taken the spoiles of the city, he set it on fire, and pulled downe the houses, and walles of it on every side.
But the women & children tooke they captive, and possessed the cattell.
Then built they the city of Dauid with a great and strong wall, with mightie towers, and made it a strong hold for them,
And they put in it a sinfull nation, wicked men, and fortified in it.
They stored it also with armour and food, and when they had gathered together the spoiles of Jerusalem, they layd them up there, and so they became a sore snare:
For it was a place to lie in wait against the Sanctuary, and an evil aduersary to Israel.
Thus they shed innocent blood on every side of the Sanctuary, and defiled it.
In so much that the inhabitants of Jerusalem fledde because of them, whereupon was made an habitation of strangers, & became strange to those that were borne in her, and her own children left her:
Her Sanctuary was laid waste like a wildernesse, her feasts were turned into mourning, her Sabbaths into reproch, her honor into contempt.
As had bene her glory, so was her dishonour encreased, and her excellencie was turned into mourning.
Moreouer king Antiochus wrote to his whole kingdom, that all should be one people,
And every one should leaue his lawes: so all the heathen agreed, according to the commandement of the king.
Indeed many also of the Israelites consented to his religion, and sacrificed to idols, and prophaned the Sabbath.
For the king had sent letters by messengers to Jerusalem, and the cities of Iuda, that they should follow the strange lawes of the land,
And forbid burnt offerings, and sacrifice, and drinke offerings in the temple; and that they should prophane the Sabbaths, and festiuall dayes:
And pollute the Sanctuarie and holy people:
Set up altars, and groues, and chappels of idols, and sacrifice swines flesh, and unclean beasts:
That they should also leaue their children vncircumcised, and make their souls abominable with all maner of vncleannesse, and prophanation:
To the end they might forget the Law, and change all the ordinances.
And whosoeuer would not do according to the commandement of the king he should die.
In the self same maner wrote he to his whole kingdom, and appointed ouerseers over all the people, commanding the cities of Iuda to sacrifice, city by city.
Then many of the people were gathered to them, to wit, every one that forsooke the Lawe, and so they committed euils in the land:
And droue the Israelites into secret places, euen wheresoeuer they could flie for succour.

Now the fifteenth day of the month Casleu, in the hundredth fourtie and fift year, they set up the abomination of desolation upon the Altar, and built idole altars throughout the cities of Iuda, on every side:
And burnt incense at the doores of their houses, and in the streetes.
And when they had rent in pieces the books of the Lawe which they found, they burnt them with fire.
And wheresoeuer was found with any, the book of the Testament, or if any consented to the Lawe, the kings commandement was, that they should put him to death.
Thus did they by their authority, to the Israelites every month, to as many as were found in the cities.
Now the fiue and twentieth day of the month, they did sacrifice upon the idole altar, which was upon the Altar of God.
At which time, according to the commandement, they put to death certaine women that had caused their children to be circumcised.
And they hanged the infants about their neckes, and rifled their houses, and slewe them that had circumcised them.
However, many in Israel were fully resolued and confirmed in themselues, not to eat any unclean thing.
Wherfore they chose rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats, and that they might not profane the holy Couenant: So then they died.
And there was very great wrath upon Israel.

And offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings, which they had made.
Looke at what time, and what day the heathen had prophaned it, euen in that was it dedicated with songs, and cittherns, and harpes, & cimbals.
Then all the people fell upon their faces, worshipping and praising the God of heaven, who had given them good successe.
And so they kept the dedication of the altar eight dayes, and offered burnt offerings with gladnesse, and sacrificed the sacrifice of deliuerance and praise.
They deckt also the forefront of the temple with crownes of gold; and with shields, and the gates, and the chambers they renewed and hanged doores upon them.
Thus was there very great gladnesse among the people, for that the reproch of the heathen was put away.

Moreouer Judas and his brethren with the whole congregation of Israel ordained that the daies of the dedication of the altar, should be kept in their season from year to year by the space of eight dayes, from the fiue and twentieth day of the month Casleu, with mirth and gladnesse.
At that time also they built up the mount Sion with high walles, and strong towres round about, lest the Gentiles should come & tread it downe, as they had done before.
And they set there a garison to keepe it: and fortified Bethsura to preserue it, that the people might have a defence against Idumea.

Furthermore they set the loaues upon the table, and spread out the veiles, and finished all the works which they had begunne to make.

Now on the fiue and twentieth day of the ninth month, (which is called the month Casleu) in the hundredth fourty and eight year they rose up betimes in the morning, And offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings, which they had made. Looke at what time, and what day the heathen had prophaned it, euen in that was it dedicated with songs, and cittherns, and harpes, & cimbals.

Then all the people fell upon their faces, worshipping and praising the God of heaven, who had given them good successe. And so they kept the dedication of the altar eight dayes, and offered burnt offerings with gladnesse, and sacrificed the sacrifice of deliuerance and praise. They deckt also the forefront of the temple with crownes of gold; and with shields, and the gates, and the chambers they renewed and hanged doores upon them.

Thus was there very great gladnesse among the people, for that the reproch of the heathen was put away. Moreouer Judas and his brethren with the whole congregation of Israel ordained that the daies of the dedication of the altar, should be kept in their season from year to year by the space of eight dayes, from the fiue and twentieth day of the month Casleu, with mirth and gladnesse. At that time also they built up the mount Sion with high walles, and strong towres round about, lest the Gentiles should come & tread it downe, as they had done before.
And they set there a garison to keepe it: and fortified Bethsura to preserue it, that the people might have a defence against Idumea.

verses.t: Now when the nations round about heard that the Altar was built, & the Sanctuarie renewed as before, it displeased them very much.
Wherfore they thought to destroy the generation of Iacob that was among them, and thereupon they began to slay and destroy the people.
Then Judas fought against the children of Esau in Idumea at Arabattine, because they besieged Israel: and he gaue them a great ouerthrow, and abated their courage, and tooke their spoiles.
Also he remembred the iniurie of the children of Bean, who had bene a snare and an offence to the people, in that they lay in waite for them in the wayes.
He shut them up therefore in the towres, and incamped against them, and destroyed them vtterly, and burnt the towers of that place with fire, and all that were in it.
Afterward he passed over to the children of Ammon, where he found a mighty power, and much people, with Timotheus their captaine.
So he fought many battels with them, till at length they were discomfited before him; and he smote them.
And when he had taken Iazar, with the townes belonging to it, he returned into Iudea.
Then the heathen that were at Galead, assembled themselues together against the Israelites that were in their quarters to destroy them: but they fled to the fortresse of Dathema;
And sent letters to Judas and his brethren: The heathen that are round about us, are assembled together against us to destroy us;
And they are preparing to come and take the fortresse whereunto we are fled, Timotheus being captaine of their host.
Come now therefore and deliuer us from their handes, for many of us are slaine.

Indeed all our brethren that were in the places of Tobie, are put to death, their wiues and their children; Also they have caried away captiues, and borne away their stuffe, and they have destroied there about a thousand men.
While these letters were yet reading, look there came other messengers from Galilee with their clothes rent, who reported on this wise,
And said: They of Ptolemais, and of Tyrus, and Sidon, and all Galilee of the Gentiles are assembled together against us to consume us.
Now when Judas and the people heard these words, there assembled a great congregation together, to consult what they should do for their brethren, that were in trouble and assaulted of them.
Then said Judas to Simon his brother, Choose you out men, and go, and deliuer your brethren that are in Galilee, for I and Ionathan my brother, will go into the countrey of Galaad.
So he left Joseph the son of Zacharias, and Azarias captaines of the people, with the remnant of the hoste in Iudea to keepe it,
To whom he gaue commandement, saying, Take you the charge of this people, and see that you make not warre against the heathen, until the time that we come again.
Now to Simon were given three thousand men to go into Galilee, and to Judas eight thousand men for the countrey of Galaad.
Then went Simon into Galilee, where he fought many battels with the heathen, so that the heathen were discomfited by him.
And he pursued them to the gate of Ptolemais; And there were slaine of the heathen about three thousand men, whose spoiles he tooke.
And those that were in Galilee and in Arbattis, with their wiues and their children, and all that they had, tooke he away and brought them into Iudea, with great ioy.
Judas Maccabeus also and his brother Ionathan, went over Jordan, and trauailed three dayes iourney in the wildernesse,
Where they met with the Nabathites, who came to them in peaceable maner, and told them every thing that had happened to their brethren in the land of Galaad,
And how that many of them were shut up in Bosora, and Bosor, in Alema, Casphor, Maked & Carnaim (all these cities are strong and great.)

And that they were shut up in the rest of the cities of the countrey of Galaad, and that against to morrow they had appointed to bring their host against the forts, and to take them, and to destroy them all in one day.

Hereupon Judas and his host turned suddenly by the way of the wildernesse to Bosorra, and when he had wonne the city, he slew all the males with the edge of the sword, and tooke all their spoiles, and burnt the city with fire.
From where he remooued by night, and went till he came to the fortresse.
And betimes in the morning they looked up, & look, there was an innumerable people bearing ladders, and other engines of warre, to take the fortresse: for they assaulted them.
When Judas therefore saw that the battaile was begun, and that the cry of the city went up to heaven, with trumpets, and a great sound,
He said to his hoste, Fight this day for your brethren.
So he went foorth behinde them in three companies, who sounded their trumpets, and cryed with prayer.
Then the hoste of Timotheus knowing that it was Maccabeus, fled from him: therefore he smote them with a great slaughter: so that there were killed of them that day about eight thousand men.
This done, Judas turned aside to Maspha, and after he had assaulted it, he tooke it, and slewe all the males in it, and receiued the spoiles therof, and burnt it with fire.
From from there went he, and tooke Casphon, Maged, Bosor, and the other cities of the countrey of Galaad.
After these things, gathered Timotheus another hoste, and encamped against Raphon beyond the brooke.
So Judas sent to espie the hoste, who brought him word, saying; All the heathen that be round about us, are assembled to them, euen a very great hoste.
He has also hired the Arabians to helpe them, and they have pitched their tents beyond the brooke, readie to come and fight against you: upon this Judas went to meet them.

Then Timotheus said to the captaines of his hoste, When Judas and his hoste come near the brooke, if he passe over first to us, we shall not be able to withstand him, for he will mightily preuaile against us.
But if he be afraid, and campe beyond the riuer, we shall go over to him, and preuaile against him.

Now when Judas came near the brooke, he caused the Scribes of the people to remaine by the brooke: to whom he gaue commandement, saying, Suffer no man to remaine in the campe, but let all come to the battell.
So he went first over to them, and all the people after him: then all the heathen being discomfited before him, cast away their weapons, and fled to the Temple that was at Carnaim.
But they tooke the city, and burnt the Temple, with all that were in it. Thus was Carnaim subdued, neither could they stand any longer before Judas.

Then Judas gathered together all the Israelites that were in the countrey of Galaad from the least to the greatest, euen their wiues and their children, and their stuffe, a very great hoste, to the ende they might come into the land of Iudea.

Now when they came to Ephron (this was a great city in the way as they should go, very well fortified) they could not turne from it, either on the right hand or the left, but must needs passe through the midst of it.
Then they of the city shut them out, and stopped up the gates with stones.

Whereupon Judas sent to them in peaceable maner, saying; Let us passe through your land to go into our own countrey, and none shall do you any hurt, we will onely passe thorow on foote: however they would not open to him.
Therefore Judas commaunded a proclamation to be made throughout the hoste, that every man should pitch his tent in the place where he was.
So the souldiers pitched, and assaulted the city all that day, and all that night, till at the length the city was deliuered into his hands:
Who then slew all the males with the edge of the sword, and rased the city, and tooke the spoiles therof, and passed through the city over them that were slaine.
After this went they over Jordan, into the great plaine before Bethsan.
And Judas gathered together those that came behind, and exhorted the people all the way through, till they came into the land of Iudea.
So they went up to mount Sion with ioy and gladnesse, where they offered burnt offerings, because not one of them were slaine, until they had returned in peace.
Now what time as Judas and Ionathan were in the land of Galaad, and Simon his brother in Galilee before Ptolemais,
Joseph the son of Zacharias, and Azarias, captaines of the garisons, heard of the valiant actes and warlike deeds which they had done.
Therefore they said, Let us also get us a name, and go fight against the heathen that are round about us.
So when they had given charge to the garison that was with them, they went towards Iamnia.
Then came Gorgias and his men out of the city to fight against them.
And so it was, that Joseph and Azarias were put to flight, and pursued to the borders of Iudea, and there were slaine that day of the people of Israel about two thousand men.
Thus was there a great ouerthrow among the children of Israel, because they were not obedient to Judas, and his brethren, but thought to do some valiant act.
Moreouer these men came not of the seed of those, by whose hand deliuerance was given to Israel.
However the man Judas and his brethren were greatly renowned in the sight of all Israel, and of all the heathen wheresoeuer their name was heard of,
Insomuch as the people assembled to them with ioyfull acclamations.

Afterward went Judas foorth with his brethren, and fought against the children of Esau in the land toward the South, where he smote Hebron, and the townes of it, and pulled downe the fortresse of it, and burnt the townes of it round about.
From from there he remoued to go into the land of the Philistines, and passed through Samaria.
At that time certaine priests desirous to show their valour, were slaine in battell, for that they went out to fight vnaduisedly.

So Judas turned to Azotus in the land of the Philistines, and when he had pulled downe their altars, and burnt their carued images with fire, and spoiled their cities, he returned into the land of Iudea.

verses.t: About that time king Antiochus trauailing through the high countreys, heard say that Elimais in the countrey of Persia, was a city greatly renowned for riches, siluer, and gold,

And that there was in it a very rich temple, wherein were couerings of gold, and brestplates, and shields which Alexander son of Philippe the Macedonian King, who reigned first among the Grecians, had left there.
Therefore he came and sought to take the city, and to spoile it, but he was not able, because they of the city hauing had warning of it,
Rose up against him in battell: So he fled and departed from there with great heauinesse, and returned to Babylon.
Moreouer there came one, who brought in tidings into Persia, that the armies which went against the land of Iudea, were put to flight:

And that Lysias who went forth first with a great power, was driuen away of the Jews, and that they were made strong by the armour, and power, and store of spoiles, which they had gotten of the armies, whom they had destroyed.
Also that they had pulled downe the abomination which he had set up upon the altar in Jerusalem, and that they had compassed about the Sanctuarie with high wals as before, and his city Bethsura.
Now when the king heard these words, he was astonished, and sore moued, whereupon he laide him downe upon his bedde, and fell sicke for griefe, because it had not befallen him, as he looked for.
And there he continued many dayes: for his griefe was ever more and more, and he made account that he should die.
Therefore he called for all his friends, and said to them, The sleepe is gone from my eyes, and my heart fails for very care.
And I thought with myself: Into what tribulation am I come, and how great a flood is it wherein now I am? for I was bountifull, and beloued in my power.
But now I remember the euils that I did at Jerusalem, and that I tooke all the vessels of gold and siluer that were in it, and sent to destroy the inhabitants of Iudea without a cause.
I perceiue therefore that for this cause these troubles are come upon me, and look I perish through great griefe in a strange land.
Then called he for Philip one of his friends whom he made ruler over all his realme:
And gaue him the crowne and his robe, and his signet, to the end he should bring up his son Antiochus, and nourish him up for the kingdom.
So king Antiochus died there in the hundredth forty and ninth year.
Now when Lysias knew that the king was dead, he set up Antiochus his son (whom he had brought up being yong) to reigne in his stead, and his name he called Eupator.
About this time they that were in the towre shut up the Israelites round about the Sanctuarie, and sought always their hurt, and the strengthening of the heathen.
Therefore Judas purposing to destroy them, called all the people together to besiege them.
So they came together, and besieged them in the hundred and fiftith year, and he made mounts for shot against them, and engines:
However certaine of them that were besieged got forth, to whom some vngodly men of Israel ioyned themselues.
And they went to the king and said, How long will it be ere you execute judgment, and auenge our brethren?
We have beene willing to serue your father, and to do as he would have us, and to obey his commandements.
For which cause they of our nation besiege the towre, and are alienated from us: Moreouer as many of us as they could light on, they slew, and spoiled our inheritance.
Neither have they stretched out their hand against us only, but also against all their borders.
And look this day are they besieging the towre at Jerusalem to take it: the Sanctuary also, and Bethsura have they fortified.
Therefore if you do not preuent them quickly, they wil do greater things then these, neither shall you be able to rule them.
Now when the king heard this, he was angry, and gathered together all his friends, and the captaines of his armie, and those that had charge of the horse.
There came also to him from other kingdomes, and from Isles of the Sea bands of hired souldiers.
So that the number of his armie was an hundred thousand foote men, and twentie thousand horsemen, and two and thirty Elephants exercised in battell.
These went through Idumea, and pitched against Bethsura which they assaulted many daies, making engines of warre: but they came out, and burnt them with fire, and fought valiantly.
Upon this Judas remoued from the towre, and pitched in Bathzacharias, over against the kings campe.
Then the king rising very earely marched fiercely with his host toward Bathzacharias, where his armies made them ready to battell, and sounded the trumpets.
And to the end they might prouoke the elephants to fight, they showed them the blood of grapes & mulberies.

Moreouer, they diuided the beasts among the armies, and for every elephant they appointed a thousand men, armed with coats of male, and with helmets of brasse on their heads, and besides this, for every beast were ordained fiue hundred horsemen of the best.
These were ready at every occasion: wheresoeuer the beast was, and whithersoeuer þ beast went, they went also, neither departed they from him.

And upon the beastes were there strong towres of wood, which couered every one of them, and were girt fast to them with deuices: there were also upon every one two and thirtie strong men that fought upon them, besides the Indian that ruled him.
As for the remnant of the horsemen they set them on this side, and that side, at the two parts of the host giuing them signes what to do, and being harnessed all over amidst the rankes.
Now when the Sun shone upon the shields of golde, and brasse, the mountaines glistered with it, and shined like lampes of fire.
So part of the kings armie being spred upon the high mountaines, and part on the valleyes below, they marched on safely, and in order.
Therefore all that heard the noise of their multitude, and the marching of the company, and the ratling of the harnesse, were moued: for the army was very great and mighty.
Then Judas and his host drew near, and entred into battell, and there were slaine of the kings army, sixe hundred men.
¶ Eleazar also (syrnamed) Sauaran, perceiuing that one of the beasts, armed with royall harnesse, was higher then all the rest, and supposing that the king was upon him,
Put himself in ieopardie, to the end he might deliuer his people, and get him a perpetuall name:
Therefore he ranne upon him courageously through the midst of the battell, slaying on the right hand, and on the left, so that they were diuided from him on both sides.
Which done, he crept under the Elephant, and thrust him under and slew him: whereupon the Elephant fell downe upon him, and there he died.
How be it seeing the strength of the king, and the violence of his forces, turned away from them.
¶ Then the kings armie went up to Jerusalem to meet them, and the king pitched his tents against Iudea, and against mount Sion.
But with them that were in Bethsura he made peace: for they came out of the city, because they had no food there, to endure the siege, it being a year of rest to the land.
So the King tooke Bethsura, and set a garison there to keepe it.
As for the Sanctuarie he besieged it many dayes: and set there artillerie with engins, and instruments to cast fire and stones, and pieces to cast darts, and slings.
Whereupon they also made engins, against their engins, and helde them battell a long season.
Yet at the last their vessels being without food, (for that it was the seuenth year, and they in Iudea that were deliuered from the Gentiles, had eaten up the residue of the store)
There were but a few left in the Sanctuary, because the famine did so preuaile against them, that they were faine to disperse themselues, every man to his own place.
At that time Lysias heard say, that Philip (whom Antiochus the King whiles he lived had appointed to bring up his son Antiochus, that he might be king)
Was returned out of Persia, and Media, and the Kings host also that went with him, and that he sought to take to him the ruling of the affaires.

Therefore he went in all haste, and said to the King, and the captaines of the host, and the company, We decay dayly, and our food are but small, and the place we lay siege to is strong: and the affaires of the kingdom lie upon us.
Now therefore let us be friends with these men, and make peace with them, and with all their nation.
And couenant with them, that they shall live after their Lawes, as they did before: for they are therefore displeased, & have done all these things because we abolished their Lawes.
So the King and the Princes were content: therefore he sent to them to make peace, and they accepted of it.
Also the King and the Princes made an oath to them: whereupon they went out of the strong hold.
Then the King entred into mount Sion, but when he saw the strength of the place, he brake his oath that he had made, and gaue commandement to pull downe the wall round about.
Afterward departed he in all haste, and returned to Antiochia, where he found Philip to be master of the city; So he fought against him, and tooke the city by force.

Therefore he came and sought to take the city, and to spoile it, but he was not able, because they of the city hauing had warning of it, Rose up against him in battell: So he fled and departed from there with great heauinesse, and returned to Babylon. Moreouer there came one, who brought in tidings into Persia, that the armies which went against the land of Iudea, were put to flight: And that Lysias who went forth first with a great power, was driuen away of the Jews, and that they were made strong by the armour, and power, and store of spoiles, which they had gotten of the armies, whom they had destroyed.
Also that they had pulled downe the abomination which he had set up upon the altar in Jerusalem, and that they had compassed about the Sanctuarie with high wals as before, and his city Bethsura.

Now when the king heard these words, he was astonished, and sore moued, whereupon he laide him downe upon his bedde, and fell sicke for griefe, because it had not befallen him, as he looked for. And there he continued many dayes: for his griefe was ever more and more, and he made account that he should die.

Therefore he called for all his friends, and said to them, The sleepe is gone from my eyes, and my heart fails for very care. And I thought with myself: Into what tribulation am I come, and how great a flood is it wherein now I am? for I was bountifull, and beloued in my power. But now I remember the euils that I did at Jerusalem, and that I tooke all the vessels of gold and siluer that were in it, and sent to destroy the inhabitants of Iudea without a cause.
I perceiue therefore that for this cause these troubles are come upon me, and look I perish through great griefe in a strange land.

Then called he for Philip one of his friends whom he made ruler over all his realme: And gaue him the crowne and his robe, and his signet, to the end he should bring up his son Antiochus, and nourish him up for the kingdom. So king Antiochus died there in the hundredth forty and ninth year.

Now when Lysias knew that the king was dead, he set up Antiochus his son (whom he had brought up being yong) to reigne in his stead, and his name he called Eupator. About this time they that were in the towre shut up the Israelites round about the Sanctuarie, and sought always their hurt, and the strengthening of the heathen.

Therefore Judas purposing to destroy them, called all the people together to besiege them. So they came together, and besieged them in the hundred and fiftith year, and he made mounts for shot against them, and engines: However certaine of them that were besieged got forth, to whom some vngodly men of Israel ioyned themselues. And they went to the king and said, How long will it be ere you execute judgment, and auenge our brethren?

We have beene willing to serue your father, and to do as he would have us, and to obey his commandements. For which cause they of our nation besiege the towre, and are alienated from us: Moreouer as many of us as they could light on, they slew, and spoiled our inheritance. Neither have they stretched out their hand against us only, but also against all their borders. And look this day are they besieging the towre at Jerusalem to take it: the Sanctuary also, and Bethsura have they fortified.
Therefore if you do not preuent them quickly, they wil do greater things then these, neither shall you be able to rule them.

Now when the king heard this, he was angry, and gathered together all his friends, and the captaines of his armie, and those that had charge of the horse. There came also to him from other kingdomes, and from Isles of the Sea bands of hired souldiers. So that the number of his armie was an hundred thousand foote men, and twentie thousand horsemen, and two and thirty Elephants exercised in battell.

These went through Idumea, and pitched against Bethsura which they assaulted many daies, making engines of warre: but they came out, and burnt them with fire, and fought valiantly. Upon this Judas remoued from the towre, and pitched in Bathzacharias, over against the kings campe.

Then the king rising very earely marched fiercely with his host toward Bathzacharias, where his armies made them ready to battell, and sounded the trumpets. And to the end they might prouoke the elephants to fight, they showed them the blood of grapes & mulberies. Moreouer, they diuided the beasts among the armies, and for every elephant they appointed a thousand men, armed with coats of male, and with helmets of brasse on their heads, and besides this, for every beast were ordained fiue hundred horsemen of the best.

These were ready at every occasion: wheresoeuer the beast was, and whithersoeuer þ beast went, they went also, neither departed they from him. And upon the beastes were there strong towres of wood, which couered every one of them, and were girt fast to them with deuices: there were also upon every one two and thirtie strong men that fought upon them, besides the Indian that ruled him. As for the remnant of the horsemen they set them on this side, and that side, at the two parts of the host giuing them signes what to do, and being harnessed all over amidst the rankes.

Now when the Sun shone upon the shields of golde, and brasse, the mountaines glistered with it, and shined like lampes of fire. So part of the kings armie being spred upon the high mountaines, and part on the valleyes below, they marched on safely, and in order.
Therefore all that heard the noise of their multitude, and the marching of the company, and the ratling of the harnesse, were moued: for the army was very great and mighty.

Then Judas and his host drew near, and entred into battell, and there were slaine of the kings army, sixe hundred men. ¶ Eleazar also (syrnamed) Sauaran, perceiuing that one of the beasts, armed with royall harnesse, was higher then all the rest, and supposing that the king was upon him, Put himself in ieopardie, to the end he might deliuer his people, and get him a perpetuall name:

Therefore he ranne upon him courageously through the midst of the battell, slaying on the right hand, and on the left, so that they were diuided from him on both sides. Which done, he crept under the Elephant, and thrust him under and slew him: whereupon the Elephant fell downe upon him, and there he died. How be it seeing the strength of the king, and the violence of his forces, turned away from them. ¶ Then the kings armie went up to Jerusalem to meet them, and the king pitched his tents against Iudea, and against mount Sion.

But with them that were in Bethsura he made peace: for they came out of the city, because they had no food there, to endure the siege, it being a year of rest to the land. So the King tooke Bethsura, and set a garison there to keepe it. As for the Sanctuarie he besieged it many dayes: and set there artillerie with engins, and instruments to cast fire and stones, and pieces to cast darts, and slings. Whereupon they also made engins, against their engins, and helde them battell a long season.

Yet at the last their vessels being without food, (for that it was the seuenth year, and they in Iudea that were deliuered from the Gentiles, had eaten up the residue of the store) There were but a few left in the Sanctuary, because the famine did so preuaile against them, that they were faine to disperse themselues, every man to his own place. At that time Lysias heard say, that Philip (whom Antiochus the King whiles he lived had appointed to bring up his son Antiochus, that he might be king)
Was returned out of Persia, and Media, and the Kings host also that went with him, and that he sought to take to him the ruling of the affaires.

Therefore he went in all haste, and said to the King, and the captaines of the host, and the company, We decay dayly, and our food are but small, and the place we lay siege to is strong: and the affaires of the kingdom lie upon us.

Now therefore let us be friends with these men, and make peace with them, and with all their nation. And couenant with them, that they shall live after their Lawes, as they did before: for they are therefore displeased, & have done all these things because we abolished their Lawes. So the King and the Princes were content: therefore he sent to them to make peace, and they accepted of it. Also the King and the Princes made an oath to them: whereupon they went out of the strong hold.

Then the King entred into mount Sion, but when he saw the strength of the place, he brake his oath that he had made, and gaue commandement to pull downe the wall round about. Afterward departed he in all haste, and returned to Antiochia, where he found Philip to be master of the city; So he fought against him, and tooke the city by force.

verses.t: In the hundredth and one and fiftieth year, Demetrius the son of Seleucus departed from Rome, and came up with a fewe men to a city of the Sea coast, and reigned there.
And as he entred into the palace of his ancestors, so it was, that his forces had taken Antiochus and Lysias to bring them to him.
Therefore when he knew it, he said; Let me not see their faces.
So his hoste slewe them. Now when Demetrius was set upon the throne of his kingdom,
There came to him all the wicked and vngodly men of Israel, hauing Alcimus (who was desirous to be high Priest) for their captaine.
And they accused the people to the king, saying; Judas and his brethren have slaine all your friends, and driuen us out of our own land.
Now therefore send some man whom you trust, and let him go and see what hauocke he has made among us, and in the kings land, and let him punish them with all them that aide them.
Then the king chose Bacchides a friend of the king, who ruled beyond the flood, and was a great man in the kingdom, and faithfull to the king.
And him he sent with that wicked Alcimus, whom he made high Priest, and commanded that he should take vengeance of the children of Israel.
So they departed, and came with a great power into the land of Iudea, where they sent messengers to Judas and his brethren with peaceable words deceitfully.
But they gaue no heede to their words, for they sawe that they were come with a great power.
Then did there assemble to Alcimus and Bacchides, a company of Scribes, to require justice.
Now the Assideans were the first among the children of Israel, that sought peace of them:
For, said they, one that is a Priest of the seede of Aaron, is come with this armie, and he will do us no wrong.
So he spoke to them peaceably, and sware to them, saying; We will procure the harme neither of you nor your friends.
Whereupon they beleeued him: however he tooke of them threescore men, and slewe them in one day, according to the words which he wrote:
The flesh of your Saints and their blood have they shed round about Jerusalem, and there was none to bury them.
Therefore the feare and dread of them fell upon all the people, who said, There is neither truth, nor righteousness in them; for they have broken the couenant and othe that they made.

After this remooued Bacchides from Jerusalem, and pitched his tents in Bezes, where he sent and tooke many of the men that had forsaken him, and certaine of the people also, and when he had slaine them, into the great pit.
Then committed he the countrey to Alcimus, and left with him a power to aide him: so Bacchides went to the king.
But Alcimus contended for the high Priesthood.
And to him resorted all such as troubled the people, who after they had gotten the land of Iuda into their power, did much hurt in Israel.
Now when Judas saw all the mischiefe that Alcimus and his company had done among the Israelites, euen aboue the heathen,
He went out into all the coast of Iudea round about, and tooke vengeance of them that had reuolted from him, so that they dared no more go foorth into the countrey.

On the other side, when Alcimus saw that Judas and his company had gotten the vpper hand, and knew that he was not able to abide their force, he went again to the king, and said all the worst of them that he could.
Then the king sent Nicanor one of his honourable princes, a man that bare deadly hate to Israel, with commandement to destroy the people.
So Nicanor came to Jerusalem with a great force: and sent to Judas and his brethren deceitfully with friendly words, saying,
Let there be no battell betweene me and you, I will come with a fewe men, that I may see you in peace.
He came therefore to Judas, and they saluted one another peaceably. However the enemies were prepared to take away Judas by violence.
Which thing after it was knowen to Judas (to wit) that he came to him with deceit, he was sore afraid of him, and would see his face no more.
Nicanor also when he saw that his counsell was discouered, went out to fight against Judas besides Capharsalama.
Where there were slaine of Nicanors side, about fiue thousand men, and fled into the city of Dauid.

After this went Nicanor up to mount Sion, and there came out of the Sanctuarie certaine of the priestes, and certaine of the elders of the people to salute him peaceably, and to shewe him the burnt sacrifice that was offred for the king.
But he mocked them, and laughed at them, and abused them shamefully, and spoke proudly,
And swore in his wrath, saying, vnlesse Judas and his hoste be now deliuered into my hands, if ever I come again in safetie, I will burne up this house: and with that he went out in a great rage.
Then the priests entred in, and stood before the altar, and the Temple, weeping, and saying,
You O Lord did choose this house, to be called by your Name, and to be a house of prayer and petition for your people.
Be auenged of this man and his hoste, and let them fall by the sword: Remember their blasphemies, and suffer them not to continue any longer.
So Nicanor went out of Jerusalem, & pitched his tents in Bethoron, where an hoste out of Syria met him.
But Judas pitched in Adasa with three thousand men, and there he prayed, saying,
O Lord, when they that were sent from the king of the Assyrians blasphemed, your Angel went out, and smote a hundred, fourescore, and fiue thousand of them.
Euen so destroy you this host before us this day, that the rest may know that he has spoken blasphemously against your Sanctuary, and judge you him according to his wickedness.
So the thirteenth day of the month Adar, the hostes ioyned battell, but Nicanors host was discomfited, & he himself was first slaine in the battell.
Now when Nicanors host saw that he was slaine, they cast away their weapons, and fled.
Then they pursued after them a dayes iourney from Adasa, to Gasera, sounding an alarme after them with their trumpets.

Whereupon they came forth out of all the townes of Iudea round about, and closed them in, so that they turning backe upon them that pursued them, were all slaine with the sword, and not one of them was left.
Afterwards they tooke þ spoiles, and the pray, and smote off Nicanors head, & his right hand, which he stretched out so proudly, and brought them away; and hanged them up, towards Jerusalem.
For this cause the people reioyced greatly, and they kept that day, a day of great gladnesse.
Moreouer they ordeined to keepe yeerely this day, being the thirteenth of Adar.
Thus the land of Iuda was in rest a litle while.

verses.t: Now Judas had heard of the fame of the Romanes, that they were mighty and valiant men, and such as would louingly accept all that ioyned themselues to them, and make a league of amitie with all that came to them,
And that they were men of great valour: It was told him also of their warres and noble acts which they had done among the Galatians, and how they had conquered them, and brought them under tribute.
And what they had done in þ countrey of Spaine, for the winning of the mines of the siluer & gold which is there

And that by their policie and patience, they had conquered all that place (though it were very farre from them) and the kings also that came against them from the vttermost part of the earth, till they had discomfited them, & given them a great ouerthrow, so that the rest did give them tribute every yere.
Besides this, how they had discomfited in battell Philip, and Perseus king of the Citims, with others that lift up themselues against them, and had ouercome them.
How also Antiochus the great king of Asia that came against them in battaile, hauing an hundred and twentie Elephants with horsemen and chariots, and a very great armie, was discomfited by them.
And how they tooke him aliue, and couenanted that he and such as reigned after him, should pay a great tribute, and give hostages, and that which was agreed upon,
And the country of India, and Media, and Lidia, and of the goodly countries: which they tooke of him, and gaue to king Eumenes.
Moreouer how the Grecians had determined to come and destroy them.

And that they hauing knowledge of it sent against them a certaine captaine, and fighting with them slew many of them, and caried away captiues, their wiues, and their children, and spoiled them, and tooke possession of their lands, and pulled downe their strong holds, and brought them to be their seruants to this day.
how they destroyed and brought under their dominion, all other kingdomes and isles that at any time resisted them.
But with their friends, and such as relied upon them they kept amitie: and that they had conquered kingdomes both farre and near, insomuch as all that heard of their name were afraid of them.
Also that whom they would helpe to a kingdom, those raigne, and whom again they would, they displace: finally that they were greatly exalted.
Yet for all this, none of them wore a crowne, or was clothed in purple to be magnified thereby.
Moreouer how they had made for themselues a senate house, wherin three hundred and twentie men sate in counsell daily, consulting always for the people, to the end they might be wel ordered
And that they committed their gouernment to one man every year, who ruled over all their country, and that all were obedient to that one, and that there was neither enuy, nor emulation among them.
In consideration of these things Judas chose Eupolemus the son of John, the son of Accas, and Iason the son of Eleazar, and sent them to Rome to make a league of amitie and confederacie with them,
that they would take the yoke from them, for they saw that the kingdom of the Grecians did oppresse Israel with seruitude
They went therefore to Rome (which was a very great iourney) and came into the Senate, where they spoke and said,
Judas Maccabeus with his brethren, and the people of the Jews, have sent us to you, to make a confederacie, and peace with you, and that we might be registred, your confederats and friends.
So that matter pleased the Romanes well.
And this is the copie of the Epistle which (the Senate) wrote backe again, in tables of brasse: and sent to Jerusalem, that there they might have by them a memorial of peace & confederacy.
Good successe be to the Romans and to the people of the Jews, by Sea, and by land for ever: the sword also and enemie, be farre from them.
If there come first any warre upon the Romans or any of their confederats throughout all their dominion,
The people of the Jews shall helpe them, as the time shall be appointed, with all their heart.

Neither shal they give any thing, to them that make war upon them, or aide them with food, weapons, money, or ships, as it has seemed good to the Romans, but they shall keepe their couenant without taking any thing therefore.
In the same maner also, if warre come first upon the nation of the Jews, the Romans shall helpe them with all their heart, according as the time shall be appointed them.
Neither shal food be given to thē that take part against thē, or weapons, or money, or ships, as it has seemed good to the Romanes; but they shall keepe their couenants, and that without deceit.
According to these articles did the Romanes make a couenant with the people of the Jews.
However, if hereafter the one partie or the other, shall think meete to adde or diminish any thing, they may do it at their pleasures, and whatsoeuer they shall adde or take away, shall be ratified.
And as touching the euils that Demetrius does to the Jews, we have written to him, saying, Why have you made your yoke heavy upon our friends, and confederats the Jews?
If therefore they complaine any more against you: we will do them justice, and fight with you by sea and by land.

Neither shal they give any thing, to them that make war upon them, or aide them with food, weapons, money, or ships, as it has seemed good to the Romans, but they shall keepe their couenant without taking any thing therefore.

In the same maner also, if warre come first upon the nation of the Jews, the Romans shall helpe them with all their heart, according as the time shall be appointed them. Neither shal food be given to thē that take part against thē, or weapons, or money, or ships, as it has seemed good to the Romanes; but they shall keepe their couenants, and that without deceit. According to these articles did the Romanes make a couenant with the people of the Jews.

However, if hereafter the one partie or the other, shall think meete to adde or diminish any thing, they may do it at their pleasures, and whatsoeuer they shall adde or take away, shall be ratified. And as touching the euils that Demetrius does to the Jews, we have written to him, saying, Why have you made your yoke heavy upon our friends, and confederats the Jews? If therefore they complaine any more against you: we will do them justice, and fight with you by sea and by land.

verses.t: Furthermore, when Demetrius heard that Nicanor and his hoste were slaine in battell, he sent Bacchides and Alcimus into the land of Iudea the second time, and with them the chiefe strength of his hoste.
Who went forth by the way that leads to Galgala, and pitched their tents before Masaloth, which is in Arbela, and after they had wonne it, they slew much people.
Also the first month of the hundred fiftie and second year, they encamped before Jerusalem.
From where they remoued and went to Berea, with twentie thousand footmen, and two thousand horsemen.
Now Judas had pitched his tents at Eleasa, and three thousand chosen men with him.
Who seeing the multitude of the other army to be so great, were sore afraide, whereupon many conueyed themselues out of the hoste, insomuch as there abode of them no moe but eight hundred men.
When Judas therefore saw that his hoste slipt away, and that the battell pressed upon him, he was sore troubled in mind, and much distressed for that he had no time to gather them together.
Neuerthelesse to them that remained, he said; Let us arise and go up against our enemies, if peraduenture we may be able to fight with them.
But they dehorted him, saying, We shall never be able: Let us now rather save our liues, and hereafter we will returne with our brethren, and fight against them: for we are but few.
Then Judas said, God forbid that I should do this thing, and flee away from them: If our time be come, let us die manfully for our brethren, and let us not staine our honor.

With that the hoste remoued out of their tents, and stood over against them, their horsemen being diuided into two troupes, and their slingers and archers going before the hoste, and they that marched in the foreward were all mighty men.
As for Bacchides, he was in the right wing, so the hoste drew near on the two parts, and sounded their trumpets.
They also of Judas side, euen they sounded their trumpets also, so that the earth shooke at the noise of the armies, and the battell continued from morning till night.
Now when Judas perceiued that Bacchides and the strength of his armie were on the right side, he tooke with him all the hardy men,
Who discomfited the right wing, and pursued them to the mount Azotus.
But when they of the left wing, saw that they of the right wing were discomfited, they followed upon Judas and those that were with him hard at the heeles from behinde:
Whereupon there was a sore battell, insomuch as many were slaine on both parts.
Judas also was killed, and the remnant fled.
Then Ionathan and Simon tooke Judas their brother, and buried him in the sepulchre of his fathers in Modin.
Moreouer they bewailed him, and all Israel made great lamentation for him, and mourned many dayes, saying;
How is the valiant man fallen, that deliuered Israel?
As for the other things concerning Judas and his warres, and the noble actes which he did, and his greatnesse, they are not written: for they were very many.
¶ Now after the death of Judas, the wicked began to put foorth their heads in all the coasts of Israel, and there rose up all such as wrought iniquitie.
In those dayes also was there a very great famine, by reason whereof the countrey reuolted, and went with them.
Then Bacchides chose the wicked men, and made them lordes of the countrey.
And they made enquirie & search for Judas friends, and brought them to Bacchides, who tooke vengeance of them, and vsed them despitefully.
So was there a great affliction in Israel, the like whereof was not since the time that a Prophet was not seene among them.
For this cause all Judas friends came together, & said to Ionathan,
Since your brother Judas died, we have no man like him to go foorth against our enemies, and Bacchides, and against them of our nation that are aduersaries to us.
Now therefore we have chosen you this day to be our prince, and captaine in his stead, that you may fight our battels.
Upon this, Ionathan tooke the gouernance upon him at that time, and rose up in stead of his brother Judas.
But when Bacchides got knowledge of it, he sought for to slay him.
Then Ionathan and Simon his brother, and all that were with him, perceiuing that, fled into the wildernes of Thecoe, and pitched their tents by the water of the poole Asphar.
Which when Bacchides vnderstood, he came near to Jordan with all his hoste upon the Sabbath day.
Now Ionathan had sent his brother a captaine of the people, to pray his friendes the Nabbathites that they might leaue with them their cariage, which was much.
But the children of Iambri came out of Medaba, and tooke John and all that he had, and went their way with it.

After this came word to Ionathan and Simon his brother, that the children of Iambri made a great mariage, and were bringing the bride from Nadabatha with a great traine, as being the daughter of one of the great princes of Canaan.
Therfore they remembred John their brother, and went up and hidde themselues under the couert of the mountaine.

Where they lift up their eyes, and looked, & look, there was much adoe and great cariage: and the bridegrome came foorth, and his friends & brethren to meet them with drums and instruments of musicke, and many weapons.

Then Ionathan and they that were with him, rose up against them from the place where they lay in ambush, and made a slaughter of them in such sort, as many fell downe dead, and the remnant fledde into the mountaine, and they tooke all their spoiles.
Thus was the mariage turned into mourning, and the noise of their melody into lamentation.
So when they had auenged fully the blood of their brother, they turned again to the marish of Jordan.
Now when Bacchides heard of this, he came on the Sabbath day to the banks of Jordan with a great power.
Then Ionathan sayde to his company, Let us go up now and fight for our liues, for it stands not with us to day, as in time past:
For look, the battell is before us and behinde us, and the water of Jordan on this side and that side, the marish likewise and wood, neither is there place for us to turne aside.
Therefore cry you now to heaven, that you may be deliuered from the hand of your enemies.
With that they ioyned battel, and Ionathan stretched foorth his hand to smite Bacchides, but he turned backe from him.
Then Ionathan and they that were with him, leapt into Jordan, and swamme over to the farther banke: however the other passed not over Jordan to them.
So there were slaine of Bacchides side that day about a thousand men

Afterward returned to Jerusalem, and repaired the strong cities in Iudea: the fort in Iericho, and Emmaus, and Bethoron, and Bethel, and Thamnatha, Pharathoni, and Taphon (these did he strengthen with high wals, with gates, & with barres.)
And in them he set a garison, that they might work malice upon Israel.
He fortified also the city Bethsura, and Gazara, and the towre, and put forces in them, and prouision of food.
Besides, he tooke the chiefe mens sons in the country for hostages, and put them into the towre at Jerusalem to be kept.

Moreouer, in the hundred, fiftie and third yere, in the second month, Alcimus commanded that the wall of the inner court of the Sanctuarie should be pulled downe, he pulled downe also the works of the prophets.

And as he began to pull downe, euen at that time was Alcimus plagued, and his enterprises hindered: for his mouth was stopped, and he was taken with a palsie, so that he could no more speake any thing, nor give order concerning his house.
So Alcimus died at that time with great torment.
Now when Bacchides saw that Alcimus was dead, he returned to the king, wherupon the land of Iudea was in rest two year.

Then all the vngodly men held a counsell, saying, Look, Ionathan and his companie are at ease, and dwell without care: now therefore we will bring Bacchides here, who shall take them all in one night.
So they went, and consulted with him.

Then remoued he, and came with a great hoste, and sent letters priuily to his adherents in Iudea, that they should take Ionathan, and those that were with him: However they could not, because their counsell was knowen to them.
Therefore they tooke of the men of the countrey that were authours of that mischiefe, about fiftie persons, and slew them.
Afterward Ionathan and Simon, and they that were with him, got them away to Bethbasi, which is in the wildernesse, and they repaired the decayes of it, and made it strong.
Which thing when Bacchides knew, he gathered together all his host, and sent word to them that were of Iudea.
Then went he and laid siege against Bethbasi, & they fought against it a long season, and made engines of warre.
But Ionathan left his brother Simon in the city, and went forth himself into the countrey, and with a certaine number went he forth.
And he smote Odonarkes and his brethren, and the children of Phasiron in their tent.
And when he began to smite them, and came up with his forces, Simon and his company went out of the city, and burnt up the engines of warre,
And fought against Bacchides, who was discomfited by them, and they afflicted him sore. For his counsell and trauaile was in vaine.
Therefore he was very wroth at the wicked men that gaue him counsell to come into the countrey, insomuch as he slew many of them, and purposed to returne into his own countrey.
Whereof when Ionathan had knowledge, he sent ambassadours to him, to the end he should make peace with him, & deliuer them the prisoners.
Which thing he accepted, and did according to his demaunds, and sware to him that he would never do him harme all the dayes of his life.
When therefore he had restored to him the prisoners that he had taken aforetime out of the land of Iudea, he returned and went his way into his own land, neither came he any more into their borders.
Thus the sword ceased from Israel: but Ionathan dwelt at Machmas, and began to gouerne the people, and he destroyed the vngodly men out of Israel.

verses.t: In the hundredth & sixtieth yere, Alexander the son of Antiochus surnamed Epiphanes, went up and tooke Ptolemais: for the people had receiued him, by meanes whereof he reigned there.
Now when king Demetrius heard of it, he gathered together an exceeding great host, and went foorth against him to fight.
Moreouer Demetrius sent letters to Ionathan with louing words, so as he magnified him.
For, said he, Let us first make peace with him before he ioyne with Alexander against us.
Else he wil remember all the euils that we have done against him, and against his brethren and his people.

Therefore he gaue him authority to gather together an host, and to prouide weapons that he might aide him in battell: he commaunded also that the hostages that were in the towre, should be deliuered him.
Then came Ionathan to Jerusalem, and read the letters in the audience of all the people, and of them that were in the towre.
Who were sore afraid when they heard that the king had given him authority to gather together an host.
Whereupon they of the towre deliuered their hostages to Ionathan, & he deliuered them to their parents.
This done, Ionathan setled himself in Jerusalem, and began to build and repaire the city.
And he commaunded the workemen to build the wals, and the mount Sion round about with square stones, for fortification, and they did so.
Then the strangers that were in the fortresses which Bacchides had built, fled away:
Insomuch as every man left his place, and went into his own country.
Onely at Bethsura certaine of those that had forsaken the law, and the commaundements remained still: for it was their place of refuge.

Now when king Alexander had heard what promises Demetrius had sent to Ionathan: when also it was told him of the battels and noble acts which he & his brethren had done, and of the paines that they had indured,
He said, Shal we find such another man? Now therefore we will make him our friend, and confederate.
Upon this he wrote a letter and sent it to him according to these words, saying:
King Alexander to his brother Ionathan, sends greeting:
We have heard of you, that you are a man of great power, and meete to be our friend.

Therefore now this day we ordaine you to be the high priest of your nation, and to be called the kings friend, (and there withall he sent him a purple robe and a crowne of gold) to take our part, and keepe friendship with us.
So in the seuenth month of the hundredth and sixtieth yere, at the feast of the Tabernacles, Ionathan put on the holy robe, and gathered together forces, and prouided much armour.
Wherof when Demetrius heard, he was very sory, and said,
What have we done that Alexander has preuented us, in making amity with the Jews to strengthen himself?
I also will write to them words of encouragement dignities and gifts, that I may have their ayde.
He sent to him therefore, to this effect: King Demetrius to the people of the Jews, sends greeting:
Whereas you have kept couenants with us, & continued in our friendship, not ioyning yourselves with our enemies, we have heard of this, & are glad:
Therefore now continue you still to be faithful to us, and we will well recompence you for the things you do in our behalfe,
And will grant you many immunities, and give you rewards.
And now I do free you, and for your sake I release all the Jews from tributes, and from the customes of salt, and from crowne taxes,

And frō that which appertains to me to receiue for the third part of the seed, and the halfe of the fruit of the trees, I release it from this day forth, so that they shall not be taken of the land of Iudea, nor of the three gouernments which are added thereunto out of the country of Samaria and Galile, from this day forth for euermore.
Let Jerusalem also be holy and free, with the borders of it, both from tenths and tributes.
And as for the towre which is at Jerusalem, I yeeld up my authority over it, and give it to the high Priest, that he may set in it such men as he shall choose to keepe it.

Moreouer I freely set at libertie every one of the Jews that were carried captiues out of the land of Iudea, into any part of my kingdom, and I will that all my officers remit the tributes, euen of their cattell.

Furthermore, I will that all the Feasts and Sabbaths, & New moones and solemne dayes, and the three dayes before the Feast, and the three dayes after the Feast, shall be all dayes of immunitie and freedom for all the Jews in my realme.
Also no man shall have authority to meddle with them, or to mole any of them in any matter.
that there be enrolled among the kings forces about thirtie thousand men of the Jews, to whom pay shall be given as belongs to all the kings forces.

And of them some shall be placed in the kings strong holds, of whom also some shall be set over the affaires of the kingdom, which are of trust: and I will that their ouerseers and gouernours be of themselues, and that they live after their own lawes, euen as the King has commanded in the land of Iudea.

And concerning the three gouernments that are added to Iudea from the countrey of Samaria, let them be ioyned with Iudea, that they may be reckoned to be under one, nor bound to obey other authority then þ high priests
As for Ptolemais and the land pertaining to it, I give it as a free gift to the Sanctuary at Jerusalem, for the necessary expences of the Sanctuary.
Moreouer, I give every year fifteene thousand shekels of siluer, out of the Kings accompts from the places appertaining.
And all the ouerplus which the officers payed not in as in former time, from henceforth shall be given towards the works of the Temple.

And besides this, the fiue thousand shekels of siluer, which they tooke from the vses of the Temple out of the accompts year by year, euen those things shall be released, because they appertaine to the Priests that minister.

And whosoeuer they be that flee to the Temple at Jerusalem, or be within the liberties of it, being indebted to the King, or for any other matter, let them be at libertie, and all that they have in my realme.
For the building also and repairing of the works of the Sanctuary, expences shall be given of the Kings accompts.
Indeed, and for the building of the walles of Jerusalem, and the fortifying of it round about, expences shall be given out of the Kings accompts, as also for building of the walles in Iudea.

Now when Ionathan and the people heard these words, they gaue no credite to them, nor receiued them, because they remembred the great evil that he had done in Israel; for he had afflicted them very sore.
But with Alexander they were well pleased, because he was the first that entreated of peace with them, and they were confederate with him always.
Then gathered king Alexander great forces, and camped over against Demetrius.
And after the two Kings had ioyned battell, Demetrius hoste fled: but Alexander followed after him, and preuailed against them.
And he continued the battell very sore until the Sun went downe, and that day was Demetrius slaine.
Afterward Alexander sent Embassadors to Ptoleme king of Egypt, with a message to this effect;
Forsomuch as I am come again to my realme, and am set in the throne of my progenitors, and have gotten the dominion, and ouerthrowen Demetrius, and recouered our countrey,
(For after I had ioyned battell with him, both he, and his hoste was discomfited by us, so that we sit in the throne of his kingdom)
Now therefore let us make a league of amitie together, and give me now your daughter to wife: & I will be your son in law, and will give both you and her, gifts according to your dignity.
Then Ptoleme the king gaue answere, saying, Happy be the day wherein you did returne into the land of your fathers, and sate in the throne of their kingdom.
And now will I do to you, as you have written: meet me therefore at Ptolemais, that we may see one another, for I will marry my daughter to you according to your desire.
So Ptolome went out of Egypt with his daughter Cleopatra, and they came to Ptolemais in the hundred threescore and second year.
Where king Alexander meeting him, gaue to him his daughter Cleopatra, and celebrated her marriage at Ptolemais with great glory, as the maner of kings is.
Now king Alexander had written to Ionathan, that he should come and meete him.
Who thereupon went honourably to Ptolemais, where he met the two kings, and gaue them and their friends siluer and golde, and many presents, and found favor in their sight.
At that time certaine pestilent fellowes of Israel, men of a wicked life, assembled themselues against him, to accuse him: but the king would not heare them.
Indeed more then that, the king commanded to take off his garments, and clothe him in purple: and they did so.

Also he made him sit by himself, and said to his princes, Go with him into the midst of the city, and make proclamation, that no man complaine against him of any matter, and that no man troble him for any maner of cause.
Now when his accusers sawe that he was honoured according to the proclamation, and clothed in purple, they fled all away.
So the king honoured him, and wrote him among his chiefe friends, and made him a duke, and partaker of his dominion.
Afterward Ionathan returned to Jerusalem with peace and gladnes.
Furthermore, in the hundredth threescore and fifth year, came Demetrius son of Demetrius, out of Crete into the land of his fathers.
Whereof when king Alexander heard tell, he was right sory, and returned into Antioch.

Now when king Demetrius heard of it, he gathered together an exceeding great host, and went foorth against him to fight. Moreouer Demetrius sent letters to Ionathan with louing words, so as he magnified him. For, said he, Let us first make peace with him before he ioyne with Alexander against us. Else he wil remember all the euils that we have done against him, and against his brethren and his people.

Therefore he gaue him authority to gather together an host, and to prouide weapons that he might aide him in battell: he commaunded also that the hostages that were in the towre, should be deliuered him.

Then came Ionathan to Jerusalem, and read the letters in the audience of all the people, and of them that were in the towre. Who were sore afraid when they heard that the king had given him authority to gather together an host. Whereupon they of the towre deliuered their hostages to Ionathan, & he deliuered them to their parents.

This done, Ionathan setled himself in Jerusalem, and began to build and repaire the city. And he commaunded the workemen to build the wals, and the mount Sion round about with square stones, for fortification, and they did so.

Then the strangers that were in the fortresses which Bacchides had built, fled away: Insomuch as every man left his place, and went into his own country. Onely at Bethsura certaine of those that had forsaken the law, and the commaundements remained still: for it was their place of refuge.

Now when king Alexander had heard what promises Demetrius had sent to Ionathan: when also it was told him of the battels and noble acts which he & his brethren had done, and of the paines that they had indured, He said, Shal we find such another man? Now therefore we will make him our friend, and confederate. Upon this he wrote a letter and sent it to him according to these words, saying: King Alexander to his brother Ionathan, sends greeting:

We have heard of you, that you are a man of great power, and meete to be our friend. Therefore now this day we ordaine you to be the high priest of your nation, and to be called the kings friend, (and there withall he sent him a purple robe and a crowne of gold) to take our part, and keepe friendship with us. So in the seuenth month of the hundredth and sixtieth yere, at the feast of the Tabernacles, Ionathan put on the holy robe, and gathered together forces, and prouided much armour.

Wherof when Demetrius heard, he was very sory, and said, What have we done that Alexander has preuented us, in making amity with the Jews to strengthen himself? I also will write to them words of encouragement dignities and gifts, that I may have their ayde. He sent to him therefore, to this effect: King Demetrius to the people of the Jews, sends greeting: Whereas you have kept couenants with us, & continued in our friendship, not ioyning yourselves with our enemies, we have heard of this, & are glad:

Therefore now continue you still to be faithful to us, and we will well recompence you for the things you do in our behalfe, And will grant you many immunities, and give you rewards. And now I do free you, and for your sake I release all the Jews from tributes, and from the customes of salt, and from crowne taxes, And frō that which appertains to me to receiue for the third part of the seed, and the halfe of the fruit of the trees, I release it from this day forth, so that they shall not be taken of the land of Iudea, nor of the three gouernments which are added thereunto out of the country of Samaria and Galile, from this day forth for euermore.

Let Jerusalem also be holy and free, with the borders of it, both from tenths and tributes. And as for the towre which is at Jerusalem, I yeeld up my authority over it, and give it to the high Priest, that he may set in it such men as he shall choose to keepe it. Moreouer I freely set at libertie every one of the Jews that were carried captiues out of the land of Iudea, into any part of my kingdom, and I will that all my officers remit the tributes, euen of their cattell.

Furthermore, I will that all the Feasts and Sabbaths, & New moones and solemne dayes, and the three dayes before the Feast, and the three dayes after the Feast, shall be all dayes of immunitie and freedom for all the Jews in my realme. Also no man shall have authority to meddle with them, or to mole any of them in any matter. that there be enrolled among the kings forces about thirtie thousand men of the Jews, to whom pay shall be given as belongs to all the kings forces.

And of them some shall be placed in the kings strong holds, of whom also some shall be set over the affaires of the kingdom, which are of trust: and I will that their ouerseers and gouernours be of themselues, and that they live after their own lawes, euen as the King has commanded in the land of Iudea. And concerning the three gouernments that are added to Iudea from the countrey of Samaria, let them be ioyned with Iudea, that they may be reckoned to be under one, nor bound to obey other authority then þ high priests

As for Ptolemais and the land pertaining to it, I give it as a free gift to the Sanctuary at Jerusalem, for the necessary expences of the Sanctuary. Moreouer, I give every year fifteene thousand shekels of siluer, out of the Kings accompts from the places appertaining. And all the ouerplus which the officers payed not in as in former time, from henceforth shall be given towards the works of the Temple. And besides this, the fiue thousand shekels of siluer, which they tooke from the vses of the Temple out of the accompts year by year, euen those things shall be released, because they appertaine to the Priests that minister.

And whosoeuer they be that flee to the Temple at Jerusalem, or be within the liberties of it, being indebted to the King, or for any other matter, let them be at libertie, and all that they have in my realme. For the building also and repairing of the works of the Sanctuary, expences shall be given of the Kings accompts. Indeed, and for the building of the walles of Jerusalem, and the fortifying of it round about, expences shall be given out of the Kings accompts, as also for building of the walles in Iudea.

Now when Ionathan and the people heard these words, they gaue no credite to them, nor receiued them, because they remembred the great evil that he had done in Israel; for he had afflicted them very sore. But with Alexander they were well pleased, because he was the first that entreated of peace with them, and they were confederate with him always.

Then gathered king Alexander great forces, and camped over against Demetrius. And after the two Kings had ioyned battell, Demetrius hoste fled: but Alexander followed after him, and preuailed against them. (For after I had ioyned battell with him, both he, and his hoste was discomfited by us, so that we sit in the throne of his kingdom)
Now therefore let us make a league of amitie together, and give me now your daughter to wife: & I will be your son in law, and will give both you and her, gifts according to your dignity.

Then Ptoleme the king gaue answere, saying, Happy be the day wherein you did returne into the land of your fathers, and sate in the throne of their kingdom. And now will I do to you, as you have written: meet me therefore at Ptolemais, that we may see one another, for I will marry my daughter to you according to your desire. So Ptolome went out of Egypt with his daughter Cleopatra, and they came to Ptolemais in the hundred threescore and second year.
Where king Alexander meeting him, gaue to him his daughter Cleopatra, and celebrated her marriage at Ptolemais with great glory, as the maner of kings is.

At that time certaine pestilent fellowes of Israel, men of a wicked life, assembled themselues against him, to accuse him: but the king would not heare them. Indeed more then that, the king commanded to take off his garments, and clothe him in purple: and they did so.

Also he made him sit by himself, and said to his princes, Go with him into the midst of the city, and make proclamation, that no man complaine against him of any matter, and that no man troble him for any maner of cause.

And tooke siluer and gold, and rayment, and diuers presents besides, and went to Ptolemais, to the king, where he found favor in his sight.
And though certaine vngodly men of the people, had made complaints against him,
Yet the king entreated him as his predecessors had done before, & promoted him in the sight of all his friends,
And confirmed him in the high priesthood, and in all the honours that he had before, and gaue him preeminence among his chiefe friends.
